q: In the Business in Context model, business activities are shaped by their contexts but have no influence on them.
why: The model stresses two-way interaction: contexts shape activities and activities shape contexts.

q: Which of these is NOT one of the five business activities in the model?
why: The five are innovation, operations, marketing, HRM, and finance and accounting.

q: The ____ approach views business as inputs from the environment, internal processes and outputs.
why: This is the systems approach.

q: According to the contingency approach, the most successful businesses are those that…
o: follow one universal set of best practices
are organized to take advantage of their environment
why: Contingency theory says there is no single best way; fit with the environment matters.

q: The book treats schools, hospitals and charities as businesses.
why: Business is defined broadly to include not-for-profit organizations.

q: Which three levels of context surround business activities in the model?
why: Strategic, organizational and environmental, all set within globalization.

q: The growth of globalization has been steady and uninterrupted since the 19th century.
why: There was a marked slowdown between 1914 and 1950, and again early in the 21st century.

q: Which perspective emphasizes the uneven distribution of benefits, the power of big business and environmental damage?
why: These are the core criticisms of the anti-globalization lobby.

q: Splitting a production process across firms in different countries is known as the global ____.
why: The global factory disaggregates production, mainly to reduce costs.

q: Compared with a traditional MNE, a transnational corporation's primary objectives are…
why: In a TNC, flexibility, responsiveness and innovation replace control and cost.

q: Joint ventures usually involve some element of shared ownership.
why: For example, two firms setting up a new company together.

q: Which development has driven the rapid growth of globalization since about 1980?
why: Information and communications technology accelerated globalization.

q: What does PEST stand for?
why: PEST: political, economic, social and technological factors.

q: In the book's definition, the state includes the judiciary, civil service, armed forces and police.
why: The state is broader than the government alone.

q: The WTO emerged from the ____.
acc: general agreement on tariffs and trade
why: The GATT was replaced by the WTO.

q: Which three broad groups of market economies does the book identify?
why: Anglo-Saxon, social market and Asian models.

q: Predictions discussed in the book indicate India will be the world's largest economy by 2040.
why: The predictions point to China.

q: GDP per capita is calculated by…
o: dividing GNP by the number of firms
why: Per capita means per head of population.

q: The book argues that technology simply determines how businesses operate, leaving managers no choice.
why: Technology is both a determinant and a product of management choice.

q: Work on self-employed contracts with no guaranteed hours is called the ____ economy.
why: The gig economy has grown in many countries.

q: Where has the impact of e-commerce been greatest?
why: Business-to-business transactions.

q: Trade union membership has increased in most countries.
why: Membership and influence have declined in most countries.

q: Labour mobility in the sense of people moving to another country…
o: is the main driver of globalization
why: Jobs move around the world more than people do.

q: What was the main effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on technology and work?
why: Much of the change was an acceleration of existing trends.

q: The primary drivers of convergence are…
why: Technology transfer and the activities of multinationals.

q: In Hofstede's survey, the USA had the highest individualism rating of any country.
why: The USA scored highest on individualism.

q: Hofstede's dimension measuring discomfort with ambiguity is uncertainty ____.
why: Uncertainty avoidance.

q: In Anglo-Saxon capitalism, the main stakeholders are seen as…
why: Shareholders are the main stakeholders in the liberal market model.

q: The varieties of capitalism approach contrasts…
why: Liberal market economies versus coordinated market economies.

q: The national business systems model is associated with Whitley.
why: Whitley's model explains differences in business systems between countries.

q: Which is NOT one of the organizational elements in the model?
why: The elements are goals, structure, ownership, size and culture.

q: In the agency problem, managers are the ____ of shareholders.
why: Shareholders are principals; managers are their agents.

q: The evidence linking organization structure to performance is conclusive.
why: The book says the evidence is inconclusive.

q: In a multidivisional company, business units…
o: operate as profit centres coordinated by a corporate HQ
must all do the same activity
why: Profit centres coordinated centrally.

q: The book defines corporate culture as a culture deliberately created by management for strategic ends.
why: Organizational culture grows naturally; corporate culture is designed by management.

q: Privatization was especially prevalent in the UK during…
why: Driven by belief in free markets in the 1980s and 1990s.

q: A common short definition of management is…
o: getting things done through other people
why: Management is getting things done through other people.

q: Leadership focuses on coordination, while management focuses on inspiring people.
why: It's the other way round.

q: Which French writer is associated with the classical principles of management?
why: Henri Fayol.

q: Studying five senior executives, ____ identified ten managerial roles in three categories.
why: Mintzberg (1973): interpersonal, informational and decisional roles.

q: The chapter concludes that management and leadership are best viewed within their organizational and environmental context.
why: This follows the Business in Context model.

q: A manager's legitimacy is based on…
o: property rights, laws, power and values
why: Several sources together give managers their right to manage.

q: SWOT stands for strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and ____.
why: Threats.

q: Porter's value chain divides activities into…
why: Primary and support activities.

q: In the BCG matrix, a product with high market share in a low-growth market is a…
why: Cash cows fund question marks and stars.

q: Backward integration means gaining control of distribution and retailing.
why: That is forward integration; backward means moving towards suppliers.

q: Strategic options should be assessed on…
why: Suitability, feasibility and acceptability to stakeholders.

q: A hotel chain buying a newspaper is an example of related diversification.
why: It is unrelated diversification.

q: CSR is concerned primarily with the firm's relationships with its…
why: Shareholders, employees, customers, suppliers, community and government.

q: The evidence that ethical business is more profitable is strong and consistent.
why: The book calls it weak and contradictory.

q: Business ethics sets the framework for the operation of ____.
why: CSR is the application of business ethics.

q: The argument that firms should be responsible simply because it is right is the…
why: The moral argument.

q: Standards of business ethics vary between cultures and over time.
why: Ethics depends on individual values, culture, norms and law.

q: Carroll's pyramid of CSR includes economic, legal, ethical and…
why: Philanthropic (discretionary) responsibilities sit at the top.

q: ____ is the discovery or creation of a product or process; innovation turns it into a business reality.
why: Invention versus innovation.

q: In most countries a patent gives a monopoly for…
why: Usually 20 years.

q: There is clear evidence that larger firms are always more innovative.
why: No clear link, though very expensive research is concentrated in large firms.

q: Demand–pull innovation comes from…
why: Demand–pull is driven by the market.

q: Tacit knowledge is…
o: rarely documented and hard for outsiders to copy
why: That's why it is a source of competitive advantage.

q: More innovative firms tend to take an open approach, with partnerships and information exchange.
why: Open innovation is associated with more innovative firms.

q: Which is NOT one of the objectives of operations management?
why: The objectives are quality, dependability, speed, flexibility and cost.

q: Because JIT starts from customer demand and works backwards, it is called a ____-through system.
why: A pull-through system.

q: The Kanban technique was developed by…
why: Toyota.

q: The operations function exists only in manufacturing.
why: It exists in all kinds of organizations, including services.

q: Benchmarking means…
o: improving quality by comparing with other organizations
why: Learning from the practices of others.

q: Lean production integrates JIT and TQM.
why: Along with flexible manufacturing and close supplier links.

q: The 4Ps classification is credited to…
why: McCarthy (1960).

q: The view that good-quality goods will sell themselves is the…
why: Product orientation, dominant until the 1950s.

q: Breaking the total market into distinct consumer groups is called ____.
why: Segmentation, followed by targeting and positioning.

q: Consumerism is a social movement that informs consumers and acts as a pressure group.
why: Consumer groups act as watchdogs.

q: Drucker claimed marketing is a narrow, specialized activity.
why: He argued marketing encompasses all the firm's activities.

q: Social media marketing shifts the marketing focus towards…
why: Consumers share opinions with each other.

q: HRM emerged as a concept…
why: 1980s, initially in the USA.

q: Recruitment and selection methods should be reliable and ____.
why: Reliability and validity.

q: Which is NOT one of the four HRM activities in the book?
why: The fourth is pay and performance.

q: Diversity management is more proactive than equal opportunities and focuses on individuals rather than groups.
why: That is how the book distinguishes them.

q: Ulrich is known for describing HR as a…
why: HR as a business partner.

q: It is easy to prove that HR strategies contribute to organizational success.
why: Their contribution is difficult to demonstrate.

q: The three parts of the finance and accounting function are…
o: financial management, management accounting, financial reporting
why: Financial management, management accounting and financial reporting.

q: The book says share capital is the most significant source of finance for UK firms.
why: Internally generated funds (reinvested profit) appear most significant.

q: A common investment appraisal technique is net present ____ (NPV).
why: Net present value.

q: A balance sheet shows…
o: assets and liabilities at the end of the accounting year
why: A snapshot of assets and liabilities.

q: A firm with a healthy order book can still fail because of poor cash flow.
why: Without cash it cannot pay its bills.

q: Transfer pricing is a particularly useful tool for…
why: Multinationals price transfers between their units across countries.
